sources.entry: RAGFlow | RAG engine built on deep document understanding

summary.one_liner: RAGFlow is an open-source Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) engine that combines document parsing, agentic retrieval, and agent templates to serve as a context layer for LLMs.
summary.what_it_does: RAGFlow ingests unstructured documents such as Word, PowerPoint, Excel, TXT, images, PDFs, scanned copies, web pages, and structured data, using deep document understanding to extract knowledge. It splits content with selectable chunking templates and lets users visualize and adjust chunks. Retrieval supports multiple recall methods with fused re-ranking, and an agentic mode performs multi-step retrieval with Low, Medium, High, or Ultra thinking modes. Answers include traceable citations to source references. The README also describes knowledge compilation, which generates wikis, graphs, trees, PageIndex, mind maps, timelines, and skills from documents or datasets, plus data source ingestion and synchronization (for example Google BigQuery and sitemaps). Configurable LLMs and embedding models are added through the web UI, and intuitive APIs are offered for integration.
use_cases: build a question-answering system over company documents
chat with PDFs and scanned files
retrieve cited answers from a private knowledge base
parse complex documents for LLM retrieval
create wikis or mind maps from document collections
sync web pages or BigQuery data into a searchable knowledge base
how_to_run: git clone the ragflow repository and cd into ragflow/docker
curl -f the server HTTP endpoint to confirm readiness, then open the Web UI in a browser
Add an LLM, embedding model, and reranker on the model provider page after sign-in
notable: Knowledge Compilation generates wikis, graphs, trees, PageIndex, mind maps, timelines, and skills from documents
Agentic retrieval with Low, Medium, High, and Ultra thinking modes
Chunking visualization that allows human intervention
Separate Admin, Ingestor, Syncer, and API services that can be launched individually
caveats: Recommended at least 4 CPU cores, 16 GB RAM, and 50 GB disk; heavier with local models
macOS is stated as not currently supported
Source builds need Go 1.27, Clang 20, LLD 20, CMake 4.0+, PCRE2, and native libraries via a download script
Elasticsearch requires vm.max_map_count set to at least 262144 on the host
DeepDoc uses CPU inference in the open-source 1.0 release
